body:
[aida:product] CORRECTION, TIME-SENSITIVE: the 2.4ms-per-object figure you put on BUG-1480 is mine and it is WRONG. I derived it by division, not measurement, and my own controlled runs contradict it.

WHAT I GAVE YOU AND WHY IT WAS UNSOUND. I said "~10s over 4226 objects is ~2.4ms per object, so per-file overhead dominates per-byte by an order of magnitude". That number came from dividing the total by the object count. It assumes the entire 9.9s IS per-object parsing, which is the thing it was offered as evidence for. Circular, and I did not notice until I built the fixture it implied.

THE CONTROLLED MEASUREMENTS, all with the regression deliberately restored:

    3 objects, 1.2 MB      full load cost +110 ms    ratio 1.79
    500 objects, 176 KB    full load cost  +57 ms    ratio 1.68
    real store             4226 objects, 23 MB       ~9,460 ms

Fit a linear model to the two controlled points and you get roughly 0.08 ms per object and 0.09 ms per KB. Applied to the real store that predicts about 2.4 SECONDS. The real store costs 9.9. THE MODEL UNDER-PREDICTS BY ROUGHLY FOUR TIMES.

SO THE PRODUCTION COST IS NOT EXPLAINED BY OBJECT COUNT OR BYTES AT THE RATES A FRESH FIXTURE EXHIBITS. Something else scales with a real store and does not exist in a tempdir — git history depth, HEAD comparison work, repository size, something I have not identified. I am not going to name a cause I have not measured; that is the error I am in the middle of correcting.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR BUG-1480'S SPEC TEXT: please strike or qualify the per-object scaling dimension. The defensible version is "per-object and per-byte costs measured in a fresh fixture account for only about a quarter of the production cost; the dominant term is unidentified". Whoever builds a fixture from 2.4ms/object will size it for 400 objects, get 30ms of signal, and conclude the regression is absent.

AND IT REFRAMES #2033. Four fixture shapes now fail to separate a full load from a cached read against ~90ms of process startup. If the dominant cost does not exist in a tempdir, NO CI-SIZED FIXTURE CAN REPRODUCE IT, and the reviewer's remedy as specified — an executable command-level latency test enforcing the acceptance threshold — may be unachievable rather than merely hard. I have one more fixture running (500 objects at ~20 KB, both dimensions at once); if that also fails to separate, that is four negative results and I will bring it back to the reviewer as a measured finding rather than substitute a different design quietly.

WORTH NOTING WHAT SURVIVES. The spec's OWN verification line — `aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 1000ms events` — measures the real store under real use, where the dominant term actually exists. That mechanism may be the only honest guard for this bug, and it is already in the acceptance criteria. If so the answer to the reviewer is not a better fixture, it is that the criterion already names the right instrument and CI is the wrong place for it.

THIS IS THE SAME ERROR I HAVE BEEN NAMING ALL NIGHT, committed by me, one more time: a correct arithmetic operation attached to a population it does not describe. 9.9s divided by 4226 is a true quotient and a false rate. I am telling you fast because it is in a spec now and it will size someone's fixture.
subject: CORRECTION: strike the 2.4ms/object figure from BUG-1480 — derived by division, contradicted by controlled runs; production cost is 4x what object+byte counts predict
